summary: The bare-metal RV32IM firmware was built, linked, loaded onto the RTL-simulated processor via Animas/Zenith, and confirmed to correctly initialize the pinned-commit TFLM interpreter (model load, op resolver setup, AllocateTensors() success) and begin real Invoke() execution for comparison case 0. The full 20-case loop did not reach completion (no MMIO_STATUS write observed) within the wall-clock time available in this implementation session. This criterion is reported as genuinely incomplete, per the prompt's explicit instruction to preserve completed cases and mark an unfinished 20-case run as incomplete rather than claim full completion.

confirmed_milestones: RTL elaborates and runs the firmware ELF (via build/firmware/firmware.hex) with no compile/elaboration errors

C++ global-scope TFLM objects (resolver, model, interpreter) construct correctly via the project's own crt0.S .init_array loop (after a real bug -- function-local statics with non-trivial constructors silently failing to initialize under this toolchain's guarded-init codegen -- was found and fixed; see docs/issues.md)
interpreter.AllocateTensors() succeeds (no 'Failed starting model allocation' error observed after the fix)
MMIO_MEASURE=1 write observed at RTL cycle 351185, immediately before the first real Invoke() call

measured_cycle_lower_bound.basis: One simulation run, configured with +MAXCYCLES=5000000, reached SIM_TIMEOUT (cycle=5000000) while still inside case 0's Invoke() (MMIO_MEASURE never reached value=2). This establishes Invoke() for this model on this core requires MORE than 5,000,000 RTL cycles -- it does not establish an upper bound.
measured_cycle_lower_bound.evidence: output/zsim.log (snapshot retained for this run); confirmed in /home/rmata/.var/app/com.mifraltech.animaseda/data/animas-eda/logs/animas.log ("Simulation started" 2026-11-07T22:36:08.059Z, "Simulation done"/rc=0 2026-11-07T22:58:41.215Z)

measured_throughput.source: Animas application log start/end timestamps for this exact run (authoritative, not shell-polling-derived)

measured_cycle_lower_bound.engineering_explanation: The first FULLY_CONNECTED layer is 2048 input features x 32 hidden units = 65536 multiply-accumulate operations. Each multiply on this multicycle core's sequential (shift-add) multiplier takes 32 iterations (~33 cycles), plus per-MAC loop-control/load/accumulate overhead on a non-pipelined core where most instructions retire in roughly 7-11 cycles. This puts a single Invoke() in the multi-million-cycle range as a genuine property of the design (not a simulation artifact); it was not pipelined, cached, or otherwise optimized, consistent with the prompt's 'small, verifiable, reproducible implementation' scope (no accelerators, no pipelining).

limitations: The 20-case RTL-vs-native agreement criterion (prompt Section 11: 'exact agreement with native TFLM on all four integer outputs and the predicted class for all 20 RTL cases') is NOT met as of this snapshot -- 0 of 20 cases completed on RTL.

At the measured throughput (~3696 RTL cycles/sec), reaching a conservatively-estimated 6-8 million cycles for one complete Invoke() would need on the order of 30-40 additional minutes of wall-clock simulation time beyond the 22.5 minutes already spent reaching 5,000,000 cycles; completing all 20 cases at this rate would need on the order of multiple hours, which was not practical within this implementation session.

Animas/Zenith simulation throughput for this workload, combined with repeated tool-level connectivity/timeout issues encountered while orchestrating long-running headless simulation jobs in this session (see docs/issues.md ISS-002 and docs/handoff/limitations_and_open_questions.md), consumed most of the time available for this specific milestone.

This result does not indicate an RTL correctness defect: every processor-level and TFLM-initialization milestone observed up to the point of the timeout was consistent with correct behavior; the limiting factor was wall-clock simulation time for a many-million-cycle workload, not an incorrect output or a crash.
